title: 9.5 A Sub-1V, 50mV Dropout LDO Using Pseudo-Impedance Buffer with Phase-Margin Improvement Design
problem: Sub-1V analog LDOs face conflicting requirements: must supply heavy load currents (I_L) while maintaining stability under light load without Miller compensation. Current-mirror (CM) buffers used in prior designs cannot cover wide load ranges—high K ratios enable heavy I_L but degrade light I_L performance (buffer resistance increases, shifting gate pole to low frequency).
motivation: Advanced technology nodes require lower supply voltages (V_IN sub-1V) with higher performance; LDOs must handle wide load swing (light to heavy) while maintaining output voltage ripple control and phase margin.
method: Pseudo-impedance buffer replaces conventional current-mirror buffer, decoupling buffer resistance from load current dependency. Frequency-compensation strategy improves phase margin across the load range without requiring high-order compensation. Single-stage error amplifier + pseudo-impedance buffer + pass transistor structure avoids Miller compensation, maintaining stability at sub-1V.
key_novelty: Pseudo-impedance buffer enables wide load-current coverage (light to heavy) in sub-1V LDO without load-dependent phase margin degradation.
contributions: Sub-1V dropout LDO (50 mV dropout) with wide load current support
Pseudo-impedance buffer decouples buffer resistance from load current, enabling light-load stability
Phase-margin improvement design maintains stability across full load range
Single-stage architecture avoids Miller compensation complexity

metrics.other: Sub-1V operation, 50 mV dropout, wide load current range

baselines: Current-mirror buffer LDOs with high K ratio (heavy load only)
Current-mirror buffer LDOs with Gm-boosting cell (references [2-4])
limitations: Efficiency, quiescent current, and output voltage ripple specs not provided in abstract.
